title: Zariski restriction on a spectral space
statement:
Let $T$ be spectral [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $T_0\subset T$
closed. Suppose every irreducible closed subset $C\subset T$ meets $T_0$ in a
nonempty connected subset. Then restriction is a bijection

$$
  \Gamma(T,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(T_0,F|_{T_0})
$$

for every sheaf of abelian groups $F$ on the Zariski space $T$ which is
locally constant [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], i.e. locally isomorphic to a
constant sheaf. The hypothesis on $F$ cannot be dropped: for $T=\mathbf
A^1_k$, $T_0=\{0\}$ and $F$ the skyscraper sheaf at a closed point $y\neq0$
one has $\Gamma(T,F)\neq0$ and $\Gamma(T_0,F|_{T_0})=0$.

proof.text: *Step 1: the zero locus of a section is clopen.* Let $s\in\Gamma(T,F)$ and let $Z(s)\subseteq T$ be the set of points at which the germ of $s$ vanishes. The locally constant-sheaf calculation is exactly [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-zero-locus-clopen], so $Z(s)$ is open and closed.

*Step 2: injectivity.* If $s|_{T_0}=0$, then $T_0\subseteq Z(s)$. Let
$C\subseteq T$ be an irreducible closed subset. Then $C\cap Z(s)$ and
$C\setminus Z(s)$ are open in $C$ and disjoint, and $C\cap T_0\neq\emptyset$
with $C\cap T_0\subseteq C\cap Z(s)$ shows that $C\cap Z(s)\neq\emptyset$; by
irreducibility of $C$ one of the two open subsets is empty, so $C\subseteq
Z(s)$. Every point of $T$ lies in the irreducible closed set
$\overline{\{x\}}$, so $Z(s)=T$ and $s=0$.

*Step 3: surjectivity.* Let $t\in\Gamma(T_0,F|_{T_0})$. By Step 1 applied to
the locally constant sheaf $F$, each point of $T_0$ has an open neighbourhood
$V$ with $F|_V\cong\underline A$ and, after shrinking, with $t|_{V\cap T_0}$
the restriction of the constant section of $\underline A$ determined by the
germ of $t$ at a point of $V\cap T_0$; such a point exists because
$\overline{\{y\}}$ meets $T_0$ for every $y\in V$, by the hypothesis applied
to the irreducible closed set $\overline{\{y\}}$. The neighbourhoods $V$ so
obtained and the open set $T\setminus T_0$ cover $T$; on an intersection of
two of them the two extending sections agree on the part lying over $T_0$,
and by Step 1 applied to the difference of the two extensions they agree
everywhere on the intersection, because the difference vanishes on a closed
set meeting every irreducible closed subset of the intersection. The
extensions therefore glue to a section $s\in\Gamma(T,F)$ with $s|_{T_0}=t$.

*Step 4: constants.* For a constant sheaf $\underline A$ the statement is
immediate, since a nonempty spectral space has global sections $A$ and $T_0$
is nonempty by the hypothesis applied to $T$ itself. This is the case used in
the applications below.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
If $T$ is spectral, $T_0\subseteq T$ is closed, and every irreducible closed
subset $C\subseteq T$ has $C\cap T_0$ connected and nonempty, then for every
abelian sheaf $F$ on $T$ the restriction $\Gamma(T,F)\to\Gamma(T_0,F|)$ is a
bijective map.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Injectivity is pointwise. If $s\in\Gamma(T,F)$ restricts to zero, its germ
vanishes at every point of $T_0$. The zero-germ locus is open and stable under
generization. If its complement contained $x$, then the irreducible closed
$C=\overline{\{x\}}$ would meet $T_0$; the specialization map from the germ
at the generic point of $C$ to the germ at $x$ would force the latter to be
zero, a contradiction.

For surjectivity, write $F$ as the filtered colimit of subsheaves generated
by finitely many sections on quasi-compact opens. Restriction to $T_0$ and
both section functors commute with this filtered colimit, so it is enough to
handle one finitely generated subsheaf. Such a subsheaf embeds into a finite
product

$$
F\hookrightarrow\prod_{b=1}^r(i_b)_*\underline{M_b},
$$

with $i_b:C_b\hookrightarrow T$ closed and $M_b$ finite: the finite germs of
the chosen generators determine finitely many closed equalizer loci, and the
corresponding finite value sets give the displayed embedding. If $F\subseteq G$, the injectivity already proved gives

$$
\Gamma(T,F)=\Gamma(T_0,F|_{T_0})\cap\Gamma(T,G)
\subseteq\Gamma(T_0,G|_{T_0}).
$$

Thus it suffices to extend sections of one finite constant pushforward.

For $i:C\hookrightarrow T$ closed, the condition on irreducible closures is
inherited by $C$. A section of $\underline M$ on $C\cap T_0$ is constant on
each connected component. Every component of $C$ meets its closed subset,
and that intersection is connected by hypothesis, so the same constant gives
a unique section on the component. These componentwise sections agree on
quasi-compact overlaps and glue by the sheaf equalizer; pushing forward gives
the extension on $T$. Finite products, subobjects, and the filtered colimit
then give an extension for $F$. The stalkwise injectivity proves uniqueness,
so restriction is bijective. This is the expanded spectral argument at Tag
`09ZG`; no etale lifting is used.

split_report.summary: Split the detailed locally constant proof into the clopen zero-locus lemma, the finite-generation embedding into closed constant pushforwards, and the constant-pushforward restriction lemma. The imported source declaration TopCat.Sheaf.bijective_unit_app_top exists in slopmaster2 but has sorry, so it is not a finished attachment. The source's phrase 'finite value sets' is not valid for arbitrary abelian groups (the constant sheaf Z is a counterexample); the embedding child therefore states abelian groups without an unjustified finiteness claim.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $T$ be spectral [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $T_0\subset T$ be
closed with inclusion $i:T_0\to T$, and suppose every irreducible closed subset
$C\subset T$ meets $T_0$ in a nonempty connected subset. Then for every sheaf of
abelian groups $F$ on the topological space $T$, restriction (the unit
$F\to i_*i^{-1}F$ on global sections) is a bijection

$$
  \Gamma(T,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(T_0,F|_{T_0}).
$$

The key step is the following shrinking property. Let $U_1,\dots,U_m$ be
quasi-compact opens of $T$ covering $T_0$, and let $A_{jk}\subseteq T$ be opens,
reflexive ($U_j\subseteq A_{jj}$), symmetric and transitive
($A_{jk}\cap A_{kl}\subseteq A_{jl}$), with $U_j\cap U_k\cap T_0\subseteq A_{jk}$.
Then there are opens $W_j\subseteq U_j$ covering $T$ with
$U_j\cap T_0\subseteq W_j$ and $W_j\cap W_k\subseteq A_{jk}$.

proof.text:
*Step 1: specialization to $T_0$.* For $y\in T$ the closure
$\overline{\{y\}}$ is irreducible and closed, so it meets $T_0$: every point of
$T$ specializes to a point of $T_0$. If $y\rightsquigarrow z$, every open
containing $z$ contains $y$.

*Step 2: injectivity.* The stalk of $F|_{T_0}$ at $z\in T_0$ is $F_z$. If
$s\in\Gamma(T,F)$ restricts to $0$ on $T_0$, its germ at every $z\in T_0$ vanishes,
so $s$ vanishes on an open neighbourhood of each such $z$; by Step 1 that
neighbourhood contains every generization of $z$, and every point of $T$ is such a
generization. Hence all germs of $s$ vanish and $s=0$.

*Step 3: shrinking.* Let $U_j$, $A_{jk}$ be as in the statement, and put
$K_j=U_j\cap T_0$, a quasi-compact set. First, if $y\in T$ specializes to points
$w_k\in K_k$ and $w_l\in K_l$, then $y\in A_{kl}$. Otherwise the connected set
$\overline{\{y\}}\cap T_0$ would be covered by the two opens
$\bigcup_{m:\,y\in A_{km}}U_m$ and $\bigcup_{m:\,y\notin A_{km}}U_m$, both meeting
it (at $w_k$ and at $w_l$), so they would meet in a point $w$ of
$\overline{\{y\}}\cap T_0$ lying in some $U_{m_1}$ with $y\in A_{km_1}$ and some
$U_{m_2}$ with $y\notin A_{km_2}$; but $w\in U_{m_1}\cap U_{m_2}\cap T_0\subseteq
A_{m_1m_2}$, an open set, contains its generization $y$, and transitivity gives
$y\in A_{km_2}$, a contradiction.

Now let $B_j$ be the set of points of $U_j$ which are generizations of a point of
some $K_k$ but do not lie in $A_{jk}$, and put
$W_j=U_j\setminus\overline{B_j}$. The set $B_j$ is closed in the constructible
topology, and in a spectral space every point of the closure of such a set is a
specialization of one of its points. Hence, if $y$ specializes to a point of $K_j$,
then $y\notin\overline{B_j}$: otherwise some $y'\in B_j$ with $y'\rightsquigarrow y$
would specialize both into $K_j$ and into some $K_k$ with $y'\notin A_{jk}$,
contradicting the first observation. In particular $K_j\subseteq W_j$, and the
$W_j$ cover $T$, since by Step 1 every $y$ specializes to a point of some $K_j$
and then lies in $U_j$. Finally, if $y\in W_j\cap W_k$, choose $l$ with $y$
specializing into $K_l$; then $y\notin B_j\cup B_k$ gives $y\in A_{jl}\cap A_{kl}$,
and symmetry and transitivity give $y\in A_{jk}$.

*Step 4: surjectivity.* Let $t\in\Gamma(T_0,F|_{T_0})$. Since $T_0$ is closed in
the spectral space $T$, it is quasi-compact, so by the definition of the inverse
image there are finitely many quasi-compact opens $U_j$ of $T$ covering $T_0$
and sections $s_j\in F(U_j)$ whose germs at the points of $U_j\cap T_0$ are those
of $t$. Let $A_{jk}\subseteq U_j\cap U_k$ be the open set of points where $s_j$
and $s_k$ have the same germ. These sets satisfy the hypotheses of Step 3, which
gives opens $W_j$. The sections $s_j|_{W_j}$ agree on overlaps and glue to
$s\in\Gamma(T,F)$, whose germs along $T_0$ are those of $t$; so $s|_{T_0}=t$.
